questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was already living in Sweden and I've heard very good things about Lund. We are only three people left in my class at KU, so I saw it as a possibility to meet new people and actually enjoy student life.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very east, they made sure that we got all the information we needed

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A week of introduction to both the school and to life in Sweden in general and on our courses and student portals etc

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was already living in Malmö, so I didn't have to find housing

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I think that if you really want to get to know a lot of people and have a very social life you should choose a dorm.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We got a link to the courses and then we had to prioritize which courses we wanted. It was very easy and there was a guide to help.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: A 10-page guide

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: successful, i got the courses I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't stress it

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The first two courses I had was completely the wrong choice for me, but that's not the institution's fault. One thing worth noticing is that there isn't any time from the last class to the exam, so you must write them while you're still taking classes.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It's the same as KU

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The same as KU but for me personally it was bigger classes so less talking for the students, but I'm sure that's just because we're so few people in my class at KU

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Modern Danish Literature
Globalization in the Premodern World
The Religious Impact of Migration in Sweden
Diversity of the World's Languages

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
The Religious Impact of Migration in Sweden
Diversity of the World's Languages
They were so interesting and taught me a lot about languages, which I'm interested in. I learned about migration in Sweden and it was nice to finally learn about Scandinavia since I've only learned things about the Middle East. I actually liked these courses so much that they helped me choose which master I want to study.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: It's pretty cheap if you have SU, because of the exchange rate, but I was also working in Denmark, you can't survive with only SU. The only unexpected thing was 300 SEK to become a member of Studentlund which gives you entrance to the social life and clubs

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Vegetables and meat were more expensive
Alcohol and food at the student nations were cheap. 50 SEK for a meal, 30 SEK for a beer and 50 SEK for a drink.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Horse riding, several gyms, hiking, trips to Norway and Finland, parties, brunch, lunch, handball etc

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I highly recommend becoming a member of Studentlund so you can join all the parties and get cheap food.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel around Southern Sweden and in general just hang out at the student nations

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Unfortunately not as I only had classes with international students

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The Swedes are strict when it comes to alcohol and smoking

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Fika

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Bring money, participate in a lot of social activites, and don't worry, everyone is so happy and welcome

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people and having an active social student life as this is something I've been missing at KU due to corona and us being a very small class

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Participating in enough things since I had a job in Denmark where I worked weekends

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
